result.title: AlphaNIST: Emergent Assembly Skills from Binary Task Rewards
result.summary: The NIST Assembly Task Board #1 remains a challenging benchmark for learning-based methods in robotic manipulation. Over short horizons, it demands precise, contact-rich control of small, tight-fitting parts. Over long horizons, it requires recovery and coordination across extended action sequences. Demonstrations, task decomposition, and dense progress rewards have enabled research advances by providing guidance on how to assemble. But how much of the strategy must be specified? The progression from AlphaGo to AlphaGo Zero showed that RL at scale can discover superhuman strategies without prescribing how to win. AlphaNIST asks whether a sparse binary task reward and task diversity admitted by this task-agnostic reward can similarly let a robot discover how to assemble. In simulation, we train a single policy from scratch across all 20 assembly tasks on the NIST Assembly Task Board #1, reaching 98.2% overall training success without demonstrations, progress shaping, scripted primitives, or per-task tuning. The framework also trains policies to complete ten assembly pairs in a single episode without a prescribed order, with task success rewarded only when all ten pairs are simultaneously complete. The learned policies discover dexterous and planning-like behaviors: choosing grasps for later assembly, using surrounding geometry to reorient parts, and preparing one part, assembling another, then returning to finish the first without an explicit planner. For videos, see our website: https://alpha-nist.github.io/

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在仿真中仅用稀疏二元任务奖励，去除演示、进度塑形与手工基元，从零训练单一策略完成 NIST 装配板全部 20 项任务，并让策略自发出现选择抓取、借助几何重定向零件等长程规划行为。
AI.relevance_reason: 稀疏二元奖励下的长程信用分配与「无显式规划器却出现多步次序」的现象，可能为 LVR 的轨迹监督、贡献分配及 THINK/LOOK/STOP 决策提供类比线索，但属远领域，可迁移性需核查。
